clue.text: Hit by a lot of commotion, tip for your uplifting narrative

indicators.note: by means next to, so the second piece sits beside the first

parts.note: a hit is a success, as a hit record or show

indicators.note: tip for means the tip, the end letter, of the storm word is swapped for the next piece

parts.note: a storm is a great commotion, as in a storm of protest
Y is the first letter of your

explanation.surface: A newspaper item: something hit by a great fuss, and the writer adds a tip for an uplifting tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip for your' looks like advice to the reader. Here 'tip for' means the end letter of the commotion word is exchanged, and the replacement is the first letter of 'your'; 'by' just sets the two halves side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A success story is an account of someone who overcame difficulty to triumph, which uplifts its audience.

clue.text: Questionable party skirting distinctive feature

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge

parts.note: a sect = a faction or party
USP = unique selling point

explanation.surface: A dubious gathering gives a wide berth to anything that stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: USP, the marketing 'unique selling point', is the distinctive feature that a product boasts of.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is open to doubt: questionable.

clue.text: Shellfish left in river attracting punters

parts.note: the Cam, the Cambridge river famous for punting
L = left

explanation.surface: A shellfish left in a river that draws in people with punts.
explanation.walkthrough: Punters look like gamblers; here they are people steering punts, flat boats poled along the Cam at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the clam is one kind of shellfish among many.

clue.text: Government entering housing agreement

indicators.note: the phrase houses the answer within its letters

parts.note: governmENT ENTEring

explanation.surface: The state moves into the business of providing homes, by agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Government' and 'entering' look like a container instruction, but they are merely the two words the answer straddles.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, an agreement.

clue.text: Cave in America's raised volume, huge internally

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: US is the United States of America; the 's means is and links it
cc, cubic centimetres, is a measure of volume

indicators.note: internally means only the inside of the next word is kept, losing its first and last letters

parts.note: jumbo means huge, as a jumbo jet

explanation.surface: A report on an American cave whose huge internal volume has been increased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' looks like a noun for a cavern, but 'Cave in' is the phrasal verb. In a down answer 'raised' reads the letters upwards; 'huge' is JUMBO, and 'internally' keeps only its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To cave in is to give way or yield under pressure, exactly what succumbing means.

clue.text: Wind in Italy absent from one of its cities?

indicators.note: I is missing from the city's name

parts.note: Turin, a city in Italy
I = Italy, its international vehicle code; removed

explanation.surface: A question about a breeze across Italy that never reaches one of its towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as the breeze, but it is the verb that rhymes with 'find': to wind a road is to turn it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: a road that winds keeps bending this way and that.

clue.text: Discharged rifle certain to backfire

indicators.note: a word discharged of its contents keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: RiflE emptied
bound = certain, as in 'bound to happen'

explanation.surface: A gun that has been fired is sure to go wrong on its user.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharged' plays on a rifle being fired, when it asks for the rifle's contents to be discharged, leaving only R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebound is to spring back on the person responsible, to backfire.

clue.text: Fanatical members in a cult sporting hair on face

indicators.note: sporting means frolicking, so the letters of in a cult play about into a new order

parts.note: a fringe is hair cut to hang over the forehead and face

explanation.surface: Members of a cult are showing off their facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' looks like wearing a beard, but it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunatic fringe is the extreme minority of a group or movement, its fanatical members.

clue.text: Pass a critical point of recent Roth novel about pot

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go around the pot word
novel means new, so the letters of the two words are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the anagram fodder, both words taken as written
an urn is a large pot or vase

explanation.surface: A literary note on a recent novel by Philip Roth, the American author, that deals with cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book by Roth, but it is the anagram signal: RECENT ROTH rearranged to TTHECORNER, which goes 'about' URN.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn the corner is an idiom for getting past the most dangerous or difficult stage, as a recovering patient does.

clue.text: Social climber's finished with graffiti?

parts.note: as in 'time's up'
graffiti is street art: ST (street) + ART

explanation.surface: An ambitious newcomer is done for, caught spray-painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that graffiti is being described rather than defined: it is street art, with street shortened to its usual ST.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has risen suddenly in status and acts above it, a social climber.

clue.text: Heard expression of disgust by wife of former prime minister, big beast

indicators.note: the answer is what you hear when the two pieces are said

parts.note: Carrie Johnson, wife of Boris Johnson
boo, a jeer

explanation.surface: A former PM's wife is heard jeering a hulking creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Carrie Johnson is the wife of Boris Johnson, UK prime minister 2019-22. Only the sound matters: CARRIE BOO spoken is CARIBOU.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a large deer.

clue.text: Gets older wife to leave reward

parts.note: wages = reward for work
W = wife; removed

explanation.surface: An older wife is asked to walk away from her payoff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets older wife' reads as one phrase about a husband's new partner; the break comes after 'older'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean growing old, and 'gets' matches the third-person S.

clue.text: Scrap is yearly bar brawl essentially

indicators.note: bar means except, so the next piece is left out of the yearly word

parts.note: annual means happening once a year

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence, the middle letter of brawl

parts.note: the word whose middle letter is used

explanation.surface: A pub landlord describes the annual punch-up in his bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' and 'brawl' paint a pub fight, but 'bar' means except: ANNUAL loses the A at the heart of brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a law or marriage is to cancel it, to scrap it as invalid.

clue.text: Break hip at end of game

parts.note: RU = rugby union
in = fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: Someone fractures a hip as the match ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The hip looks like a body part broken in the game; it means trendy, which is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to wreck or destroy.

clue.text: Case for routinely bolstering dog food

indicators.note: in a down answer, bolstering supports from beneath, so this piece goes below

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something is regularly propping up a dog's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog food' suggests pet food, but the dog is only wordplay and food alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Curry is a spiced dish of South Asian origin, a kind of food.

clue.text: Wicket and dodgy shot at cricket club

parts.note: W = wicket in cricket scoring
an edge is a shot off the side of the bat

explanation.surface: A cricket club notes a wicket falling to a streaky shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket club' reads as one unit; the club is golf's, a wedge, and 'at cricket' belongs to the shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a golf club with a steep face for lofted shots.

clue.text: Interfere with focus of Liverpool — to stop United playing

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the letter goes inside the rearranged word
playing means in play, moving around, so the letters of United are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

indicators.note: focus of means the central point, the middle letter of the nine-letter word

parts.note: the word whose middle letter is used

explanation.surface: A football report: Liverpool's aim is to stop Manchester United playing their game.
explanation.walkthrough: In English football Liverpool and United are rival clubs. 'playing' rearranges UNITED to INTUDE, and 'to stop' plugs in R, the 'focus of' Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to butt in where one is not wanted, which is to meddle or interfere.

clue.text: Measure elder's heart murmur to check

parts.note: a breath = a whisper, a murmur

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: middle letter of elDer

explanation.surface: A doctor listens to an old person's heart murmur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart murmur' is the medical phrase the surface builds; split, 'heart' belongs to 'elder's' and 'murmur' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is a dimension, a measure of how wide something is.

clue.text: Plot to banish leading character in wild system of government

definitions.note: the adjective federal names a system of government with a central power and member states

indicators.note: in places the shortened plot inside the word for wild

parts.note: feral means wild

indicators.note: banishing the leading character drops the first letter of the plot word

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A conspiracy to exile a leader in a wild political system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a conspiracy but is a patch of garden; banishing its leading character leaves two letters for the wild word to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Federal describes a union of states under a central authority, used as in a federal system of rule.

clue.text: Gent with a doc wasting time, fabulously in shape

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the time letter comes out of the pool
fabulously means in a fantastic, unreal way, so the letters are reworked
with joins the gentleman to the doctor, setting their words side by side in one pool

parts.note: T is the physics abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A gentleman and his doctor waste time looking marvellous in fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T from GENT, then rearrange GEN with A DOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a flat figure with ten straight sides, a geometric shape.

clue.text: Well-read Listener buried in large study turned up

indicators.note: buried in means placed deep inside the letters that follow

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study or room
an ear is what listens

explanation.surface: A scholar who is all ears sits buried in a large study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listener' looks like a person, but it is the organ that listens. 'buried in' puts it inside the large-plus-study letters, which 'turned up' reverses in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person has gained much knowledge through study, so is scholarly and well-read.

clue.text: Natural skin, say, nice unclothed

parts.note: the skin is an organ, the largest in the body; 'say' marks it as an example

indicators.note: unclothed means stripped of its outer layer, so nice loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the word whose middle letters are kept

explanation.surface: A beauty ad: natural skin, as nice as it looks without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you skin is only an example of the class, which is organ. 'unclothed' strips N and E from nice to leave IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown without artificial chemicals, so it is natural.

clue.text: Put down hole with Poulter's number one iron

parts.note: O looks like a hole

indicators.note: the first letter of the name

parts.note: first letter of Poulter
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: The golfer Ian Poulter holes out using his favourite iron.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Poulter is an English golfer, so 'hole', 'iron' and 'Put' all sound like golf; the iron is for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress people is to keep them down by force: to put them down.

clue.text: Developing US stock exchange down by half, little money there

parts.words: US stock exchange down by half
parts.note: the first half of NASDAQ
a cent is a small coin in the US, 'there'

explanation.surface: Wall Street shares have halved in value, leaving hardly any cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to the US: the cent is that country's small coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into being, developing.

clue.text: Creep from Squeeze knocking off piano

parts.note: pinch = squeeze
p = piano, quietly in music; removed

explanation.surface: The band Squeeze lose their keyboard player, and someone sneaks away.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S and 'piano' suggest the band Squeeze and its keyboards; it is just the verb pinch, less the musical P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: moving forward a tiny distance at a time.

clue.text: Twists in lounge abruptly turning

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes
turning round faces the word the other way, so it reads backwards

parts.note: SPRAWL (lounge) without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone lolling about suddenly rolls over and contorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like a room; it is the verb, to sprawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: damp timber bends out of true.

clue.text: Customer with cunning manoeuvre first to finish

indicators.note: first to finish means the opening letter is moved to the end

parts.note: a ruse is a cunning trick or stratagem

explanation.surface: A shopper uses a crafty trick to be first through the checkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to finish' reads like winning a race, but it moves the R of RUSE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who uses a service or product, which is what a customer does.

clue.text: Section of song, energy to knock out one?

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
I = one, the Roman numeral; knocked out
E = energy; replaces I

explanation.surface: A section of a song has enough energy to floor someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section of song' looks like the definition; the definition is just 'Section', and 'of' belongs to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a part marked off from the whole, as a section of a field.

clue.text: Picked up pen, problem with lid

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, heard

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a pen, then struggles to get the cap off.
explanation.walkthrough: The lid is an eyelid, not a pen top, and the pen is a pig's enclosure, not for writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid.

clue.text: Lady who sings right at home producing Rocket Man

parts.note: Lady Gaga, the pop singer
R = right
in = at home

explanation.surface: Lady Gaga, relaxing at home, puts out a cover of Elton John's Rocket Man.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket Man is an Elton John song, so the music surface holds together; here it is Yuri Gagarin, the first man in space.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin rode a rocket into orbit in 1961, the first man in space.

clue.text: Ultimate in messages uncovered about short guys

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped off

parts.note: texts are phone messages
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: men are guys

explanation.surface: The last word in text messages, with nothing hidden, about some brief encounters with men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' takes the outer T and S off TEXTS to give EXT; 'short' trims MEN to ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means farthest out or most severe, the utmost degree, which is what ultimate also means.

clue.text: Red-hot in May, son visiting fair

parts.note: used as written
may = can, be permitted to
decent = fair, reasonable
S = son; goes inside DECENT after DE

explanation.surface: A scorching May, with a son going to a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month, and so 'in May' like a date; it is the verb, can. The pieces run IN + CAN + DE(S)CENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incandescent glows with heat, red-hot.
